correctness.rationale: For z=abc the only possible initial Sardinas–Patterson residual is c, requiring ab in X. A one-letter residual follows the edge p→q from each short word pq. Its only possible transition to length two is a→bc by stripping a from z. If z is nonconstant then bc differs from ab, so bc cannot be cancelled from the front of z; nor can it make any transition with a length-two word other than equality. Thus nonconstant ambiguity requires bc in X and reachability of a from c using the two edges a→b and b→c. This holds exactly when c=a (if c=b≠a the only outgoing edge from c loops; otherwise c outside {a,b} is a sink). If z is constant, aa in X suffices and is necessary by the initial prefix test. The displayed concatenations give witnesses of length five; no shorter length has two distinct feasible length patterns or more than one factorization with a fixed pattern. Counting the disjoint families as unordered short-word pairs gives q(q−1)(q+2) and the stated probability.
residual_risks: Distinct short words, a named finite alphabet, ordinary concatenation, and the exact profile (2,2,3) are essential to the proof and counting normalization.
